purpose: Derek's working faucet supplies the physical starting point for this appearance study.
tried: The assembled existing Sculpted faucet, with its display powered, flavor selection working and soda dispensed using its lever.
said: I've got it lit up, and it's functional, and I can push the lever and I get the soda, and it comes out the tip, and I can select the flavor, and it's great. I love it.
scope: The existing fixed faucet. The pull-out concept has not been made or tried.

observations.subject: Soda discharge after releasing the existing fixed faucet's lever
observations.said: I should mention, in the existing design, after letting go of the lever, there is a quick stop of the main flow, but immediately a bit of fast drip followed by slow drip for a few seconds as that soda water in the gooseneck does its thing that soda water does.
observations.observed: The main flow stops quickly, followed by fast and then slow dripping from the dispense outlet.
observations.scope: Derek's physical observation of the current fixed faucet; the pull-out hose has not been tested.

observations.subject: Pouring with the existing fixed faucet's lever pressed all the way
observations.said: I've found a lot of things work better (I can go into detail if needed, but I suspect you can infer the obvious) when I use full blast on the existing prototype. When I've had guests use it, I've told them to press the lever all the way for this reason. I think one rate is right for us.
observations.observed: The prototype pours better with the lever fully pressed, and guests are told to press it all the way.
observations.scope: Derek's physical observation of the current fixed faucet on the Lillium-fed prototype; no electric valve has been made or tried.
